READYThe buggy method is:

`com.google.javascript.jscomp.LightweightMessageFormatter.format(com.google.javascript.jscomp.JSError, boolean)`

Diagnosis:
- The failing tests expect a caret `^` to be printed even when the error column is exactly at the end of the source line.
- In `format(...)`, caret rendering is guarded by:

```java
if (excerpt.equals(LINE)
    && 0 <= charno && charno < sourceExcerpt.length()) {
```

- This excludes the case `charno == sourceExcerpt.length()`.
- The comment directly above already indicates this case is meaningful:

```java
// charno == sourceExpert.length() means something is missing
// at the end of the line
```

Dynamic verification confirmed that in the failing case:
- `excerpt == LINE`
- `sourceExcerpt == "assert (1;"`
- `charno == 10`
- `sourceExcerpt.length() == 10`

Because the condition uses `<` instead of `<=`, the code skips the branch that appends the spaces and caret line, so the formatted message is missing:

```java
          ^
```
